newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus leader hails Yeltsin's referendum proposal.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader hails Yeltsin's referendum proposal.

text.p: Belarus leader Alexander Lukashenko welcomed a suggestion by Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Monday that their countries should consider the idea of a referendum on unification.

"I am very glad the Russian president has reacted in this way," the Belarus president told reporters in the capital Minsk. "If Boris Niklolayevich is ready, you know my position -- I have long been ready."
Yeltsin sent a letter to Lukashenko on Monday calling for an acceleration of moves to integrate and raising the idea of a referendum on a merger "in one form or another."
Presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said no decision had been taken on a referendum, but it was an idea to be considered by the two former Soviet republics.
He said Yeltsin's letter had raised the possibility of Russia and Belarus having a single government, with a single budget and currency taxation laws, and united fuel and energy systems.
A Kremlin official, speaking last month on condition of anonymity, said Moscow was trying to decide how to respond to Lukashenko's own plan to hold a referendum in March.
The two Slav states signed an accord last April on closer economic and political ties and forming a loose community.
Yastrzhembsky quoted Yeltsin as saying in his letter that the community had become a reality and further, serious steps should follow to bring the two former Soviet republics closer.
